set.approach: The route is in East Gully on the north side of Garden Creek Gap. East Gully is the first gully that comes into the gap from the east, and this is the first sport climb you meet heading up it.

review.notes: Area page: first gully entering the gap from the east; route page: first sport climb met going up the gully. No parking info stated for this side. No descent stated.

set.approach: There are two ways in. From the Priest Lake side, hike the Chimney trail in to Roothaan and then follow the ridge down toward Gunsight. The shorter way is to hike into Hunt Lake, swing around Gunsight's back-left side and traverse in under the north face. The basin under the face has room for tents and snowfield melt for water, and a cable between two trees serves for hanging food. To find the start, look for the arch at mid-face, then trace the diagonal crack that descends rightward from the arch's right-hand end; the climbing starts on the right half of the shallow corner system beneath it.
set.descent_text: The route can be rappelled with doubled ropes, or you can walk off via the west ridge, then follow the grassy ramp to return to the foot of the north face.

review.notes: Area page: both approaches, camp and water; route page: start location, rappel or west-ridge walk-off. Counts omitted (single source).

set.approach: Park as for the Lion Creek water slides and pass through the concrete barricades, then look for cairns and rough paths down to the creek crossing. Past the crossing, a boulder-and-scree climb angling up and left, marked by a few cairns, takes you to the foot of the slabs. Slog up the talus and through the alders, following the cairns and yellow ribbons, until you step down to the southwest toe of the slab. The first bolt is a short way up from there, and the route sits to the right of The Lion King.
set.descent_text: The route was laid out as a rappel line down the slab, on stainless anchors. Tie knots in the rope ends, because a couple of the rappels use nearly the whole rope.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: toe of slab start, intended as a rappel line. Pitches above the slab were unfinished and are not described.

set.approach: Park in the pullouts just outside The Gap on the east side, then continue up Arimo Road on foot. The climbs are on the south side of the road, and a small creek crossing is needed to reach them. Look for the clear slab facing east on the gap's south side.

review.notes: Area page: pullouts, Arimo Rd, creek crossing; route page: east-facing slab on the south side. Several hundred meters distance omitted. No descent stated.

set.approach: The Tooth is a free-standing pillar just south of Rabbit Rock. From the saddle east of Rabbit Rock, head south to the prominent pillar and hike up a small hill to its base; walking on from the east needs a short scramble. Bucktooth is just left of Hare Lip on the north face.
set.descent_text: The route now has chains and stainless lower-offs, so lower off the anchor.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: just left of Hare Lip, chains and stainless lower-offs.

set.approach: The Tooth is a free-standing pillar just south of Rabbit Rock. From the saddle east of Rabbit Rock, head south to the prominent pillar and hike up a small hill to its base; walking on from the east needs a short scramble. Hare Lip climbs the north face and is the rightmost bolted route when you face the wall from the north.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: rightmost bolted route on the north face. No descent stated.
